newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank agrees Podnikatelska Banka's end - CTK.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank agrees Podnikatelska Banka's end - CTK.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) on Friday gave approval for its administrators of Podnikatelska Banka to settle with creditors and end the already shut private bank's existence, the Czech CTK agency reported.
"The banking committee of CNB agreed today that the administrator of Podnikatelska Banka would propose a (final) settlement," CTK quoted CNB spokesman Martin Svehla as saying.
Central bank officials were not immediately available for additional comment.
Svehla said the settlement would have to be approved by Podnikatelska's shareholders as well as by creditors and the commercial court.
He said the difference between bankruptcy and a settlement was that bankruptcy was proposed by a creditor, while "settlement" was proposed by the company itself through its general meeting.
Podnikatelska was put under forced administration in June and shut in the wake of 1995 losses of over one billion crowns ($36 million).
Podnikatelska Banka, with headquarters in Prague and five branches across the country, became the eighth Czech bank to come under the supervision of the central bank.
Since then three other banks have been put in forced administration.
The central bank lowered Podnikatelska's basic capital to one million crowns from 700 million to cover liabilities.
